contexts.text: A refiner's fire () = temptation, by means of which there is purification.
The goldsmith spreadeth it over with gold (). Explained. AC 9852:2. AC 10406:4. AE 587:4.
The work of the workman and of the hands of the goldsmith () = that which is from man's Own intelligence. AR 450:end. AE 576:7. AE 585:10. AE 1186:2.
Every evil is made up of concupiscences.
Why man is constituted of these three loves.
The matters of which the bodies of men are composed.
The internal delights which enter into the external and compose them.
Dogmas made up from man's Own intelligence... TCR 508:4.

By these words is described how doctrine is forged and framed by means of falsities; thus by means of such things as are from man's Own intelligence... By the artificer and the founder... is meant one who devises and forms such doctrine.
